intro: Intervals marked 'Official source' come from Toyota Japan's maintenance pages (or DENSO for plugs). The rest are common practice. 'Severe' means Toyota's シビアコンディション: lots of rough roads, high annual mileage, or frequent hills. UK short-trip use is worth treating as severe too.

items.note: Toyota Japan's figure for non-turbo petrol cars. Many UK owners change it every 6,000 miles or yearly. Do check the dipstick monthly on a 2AZ (see Known faults).
Same interval as the oil on non-turbo petrol cars.
Toyota Japan says every 2–3 years. 2 years is the safe end.
Toyota Japan: about every 2–3 years, or when a tester says so. Weak batteries cause power-door and smart-key oddities.
Toyota sets no interval: inspect for cracks and glazing and replace when worn (checking it yearly is our suggestion). Squealing on cold starts or with the A/C on is the usual sign.
First change at 160,000 km or 7 years, then every 80,000 km or 4 years. On an import of unknown history, change it once and then use the 80,000 km / 4 year interval.
DENSO gives up to 100,000 km for long-life types (the genuine SK and Iridium Tough VK plugs). Cheaper 'Iridium Power' (IK) plugs are shorter-life. Toyota says inspect and replace when worn.
The rear bank needs the intake plenum off, so it's a bigger job.

Toyota says 'consult a dealer' and lists no interval. Japanese garages recommend changing it to prevent judder; plenty of cars reach 150,000 km never having had it changed. On a high-mileage car with old fluid, change it gradually (a drain & fill at a time).
Sealed 'lifetime' fill. Owners do a drain & fill as preventive maintenance.
Dry runners make the power doors labour and wear the cables.
Or as soon as the key's range drops.
A UK legal requirement once the car is 3 years old.
